note: Curated from the Btown Brief newsletter vault (editions Oct 19 - Oct 30, 2026). TALKING-POINTS.md is the style doctrine; refreshes land as PRs and points age out via 'added'.

points.text: UVM's Perkins Museum of Geology has reopened after six years dark, with the Charlotte Whale — Vermont's official state fossil — back on display and student interns running the exhibits. It's free, Monday through Friday from 9 to 4. What's the strangest fossil or specimen you'd want to see under glass?

The old Charlie's Boathouse on the bike path by the Winooski River bridge is becoming a public park, with 600 feet of shoreline and a new ramp planned as phase one. What would you want to see there: a fishing dock, a picnic spot, or something else entirely?

Vermont Pub & Brewery closes for good on Nov. 14, after 38 years — Greg Noonan and the late Bill Mares actually wrote the law that made brewpubs legal in Vermont back in 1988. What's your go-to order there before last call?

Crews from Massachusetts are restoring the clock faces atop the First Unitarian Universalist church on Church Street, hand-making parts that don't exist anymore — the whole thing chimes again at noon starting Nov. 15. What sound or landmark in town would you miss most if it suddenly went quiet?
Bluebird BBQ on Riverside Avenue closed for good after 17 years and a turn on Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives. What's the one thing off that menu you'd want for one last plate?

Essex Experience, the old outlet mall Peter Edelmann turned into a hub of local shops and cafés, is up for sale at $27.75 million — though Edelmann is staying on to run Essex Cinemas and build Phun, a new entertainment center with duckpin bowling, darts and an arcade next to the Hannaford. Which game are you claiming first: the bowling lanes or the dartboards?

Milton's Barry Genzlinger, known around town as Barry the Bat Guy, has rehabilitated roughly 1,000 bats and keeps the ones people find indoors safe all winter before releasing them in spring. If you found a bat in your house tonight, are you calling Barry or handling it yourself?

Vermont's Caitlin Abrams spends her free time gently scrubbing grime off 18th and 19th century gravestones in remote cemeteries and researching who's buried beneath them — she calls it 'journalism, but for dead people.' Which old Vermont graveyard would you want her to visit next?

Vermont Green FC's Chris Taylor is stepping down as head coach after two years that included a 45-game unbeaten run, a Steinbrecher Cup and back-to-back USL2 national titles. What single game from that unbeaten run would you want to rewatch first?

Jason Fitzgerald's Sock Out Cold Feet drive has collected and handed out more than 13,000 pairs of socks for people experiencing homelessness across Chittenden County in just four years. Wool, fuzzy, or plain white tube socks — what's going in your donation bag?

After a move to the old Silver Palace fell through, El Gato Cantina reopened in Essex Junction as El Bar, with pool, darts, a simplified menu and new tamales and chiles rellenos. What's the one bar game you're always terrible at but keep playing anyway?

Burlington's fourth graders are now taking swim lessons at the YMCA during school hours — twice a week for three weeks per school — in what officials call the first program of its kind in Vermont. What skill do you wish your own school had taught you hands-on like that?

Vermont Tortilla is back in production at a new facility on Boston Court in Essex after losing its Shelburne lease and a bid in Hinesburg, with a staff of three now shipping frozen tortillas nationwide. What's the dish in your fridge that absolutely needs a good tortilla?

An 11-foot stainless steel sculpture called 'Jambo' — Swahili for hello — was just installed near the Dorset Street entrance of South Burlington's Veterans Memorial Park, donated by a local resident and valued at $80,000. What would you want a giant sculpture of, if you got to commission one for your own neighborhood?

Beta Technologies just became the first company authorized by the FAA to fly passengers in its electric aircraft, and it flew one from Plattsburgh to Burlington in 20 minutes. Where's the first short hop you'd want to try in one of those?

South Burlington's OnLogic — started at a kitchen table in 2003 — is being bought by Japan's Omron for $675 million, and every employee gets a bonus of $1,500 for each month they've worked there, up to $90,000 for a five-year employee. What would you do with a bonus like that?

A month into Colchester's diverging diamond interchange, the reviews are mostly positive, though the cones are still out and some drivers say the new signals have made things worse. Have you fully figured out the new left-turn dance yet, or are you still white-knuckling it?

Burlington's Mexican food scene keeps turning up in unlikely spots — Doña Esa is now serving mole rosa and chiles en nogada at Doma Bar on Pine Street, while Taquería Don Richard has built a TikTok following on handmade tortillas in the University Mall food court. Mall food court or Pine Street bar — where are you headed for tacos?

Breeze Airways is adding a Myrtle Beach route from Burlington next May, with a nonstop add-on to Fort Lauderdale, and the airline is teasing a new warm-weather international destination before the month is out. If you could pick Breeze's next international route yourself, where would you send it?

Starting in fall 2027, UVM Promise will cover full tuition for any admitted Vermont student from a household earning up to $125,000 a year, up from $100,000 just two years ago. What would going to college tuition-free have changed for you?

Colchester High's Juliet Wager became the first girl in her troop to reach Eagle Scout by building the Snack and Books pantry, a Little Free Library near Mallets Bay School stocked with canned goods and books. What would you stock a neighborhood pantry like that with first?

Vermont is using helicopters to haul about 3,000 pounds of steel up to rebuild the staircases on the Elmore and Spruce Mountain fire towers, century-old lookouts built by the Civilian Conservation Corps and relocated from St. Albans in 1943. Which old fire tower have you actually climbed, and which one's still on your list?
